rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Molecular basis of inheritance: DNA structure, replication, transcription, translation, gene regulation ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Molecular basis of inheritance** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Heredity and Evolution fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Heredity is chemistry. DNA was found in 1869 (Miescher), shown to be the transforming principle in 1944 (Avery), confirmed by the Hershey–Chase blender experiment in 1952, and its double helix solved by **Watson and Crick in 1953** using Chargaff's base rules and Franklin's X-ray photo.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: DNA structure in numbers: double helix, antiparallel, 2 nm wide, 3.4 nm per turn, 10 bp/turn; A=T, G≡C (Chargaff) — the numbers are the marks.  ·  Trick 2: Replication: semi-conservative (Meselson–Stahl), 5'→3' synthesis, leading continuous/lagging Okazaki fragments, DNA polymerase + helicase + ligase — one line each.

Key terms and statements Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).  ·  **Worked example — reading the code.** A template DNA strand reads 3'-TAC GGA TTA-5'. The mRNA is 5'-AUG CCU AAU-3' (U replaces T; transcription starts at the promoter, not at AUG by chance). Reading in frame: AUG = methionine (start), CCU = proline, AAU = asparagine — peptide Met-Pro-Asn.…  ·  ## 7.
